column2: Libero - accessible, themeable components for Dioxus

column3: Installing libero, wrapping an app in LiberoProvider, building for the web, natively, in a desktop WebView and for Android, and the feature flags.
The four principles behind libero in order of priority (developer experience, accessibility, batteries included, simple yet modern) and what we do about each.
The sx styling builder every component takes: theme values, states, selectors, responsive, media and container queries, cascade layers and the parts Style API.
How to customize a Libero theme and use it: colors, scales, per-component defaults, light and dark pairs, and reading the active theme.
The words components say on their own, how dates and numbers are written, and the reading direction: Localization, Formats and the hooks that switch them.
LiberoProvider (themes, localization, formats, direction) and IconProvider (glyphs): what each provides, and how parts of a page sit below different providers.
Every platform API (elements, timers, keys, scroll, the document, the colour scheme, the clock), what each enables, and what to do where a renderer lacks one.
The projects whose icons and logos libero and these docs use (Lucide, pictogram, Lobe Icons, Simple Icons, eleven more icon sets), their licences and notices.
What libero's accessibility support covers across the library and what it does not, from on and disabled states to forced colors, which is covered only in part.
Confines Tab and Shift+Tab cycling to its children, for keeping keyboard focus inside an open overlay.
A span read by screen readers but hidden from sighted layout, for extra context on something vague on its own.
An id unique within the app, stable for the component's lifetime, for the aria wiring between one instance's elements.
Puts focus back on the element that opened a panel or popup once it closes, with fallbacks for a trigger that is gone.
Reads the reader's accessibility settings and lets an app force reduced motion.
Every public libero hook in one table, with what it is for and the page that shows it.
A handle to one of your component's own elements, to focus, scroll and measure it on every renderer.
Pointer plumbing for a drag. Capture, a start point, deltas against it, and one end path for release and cancel.
Reports how much of an element is visible, with a root, margin and thresholds; never intersecting where nothing can observe.
Pointer handlers that call back once a press is held, without breaking a tap or a scroll.
Touch swipe handlers, and an edge swipe that opens a drawer without fighting Android's back gesture.
Runs a callback once or on a period, started and stopped from code, cancelled when the component unmounts.
Signals and callbacks that follow their source once it settles or at most once per period.
Undo and redo over snapshots of a value, with rapid changes grouped into one step by time or size.
Runs a handler on a keyboard shortcut from anywhere in the page, skipping text entry unless asked, and stops when the component unmounts.
Whether a CSS media query or the 768px mobile breakpoint matches, live, with a documented default where nothing can measure.
Plays and reads an <audio> or <video> you render yourself, one signal per read; the engine behind Audio and Video.
Runs a handler on Android's Back button instead of leaving the app, below any overlay opened later; does nothing elsewhere.
Puts one of your elements in fullscreen, natively or drawn as a fixed box where the platform refuses it; the engine behind Video's fullscreen.
The device's position, once or followed, with the location permission; never prompts on mount.
A value kept under a key across reloads and app runs, or for the tab's session; a file per key off the web.
A larger value kept under a key in IndexedDB, loaded and saved without blocking the page; a file per key off the web.
The camera and microphone with a preview, a PNG snapshot, a chunked video or audio recording and a camera switch; never prompts on mount.
Notifications the operating system draws and a web push subscription; never prompt on mount.
Saves bytes the app made as a file: a download on the web, a save dialog on the desktop and Blitz, the share sheet on Android.
Reads and swaps the active theme set, which a theme picker is built on.
Registers a stylesheet of your own above every libero layer and returns its class.
An icon-only button, rendered as a button or a link, with a required aria_label.
A clickable action, a toggle, or a router-aware link.
Buttons and action icons side by side as one control, sharing seams and defaults.
An icon button that copies a value to the clipboard and confirms it with a check and a spoken "Copied".
An icon button that turns the app's text between left to right and right to left.
A link to a GitHub or GitLab repository with its star count beside the host's icon.
An icon button that flips the colour scheme, optionally through the system's too, with an optional theme picker beside it.
A menu of links that ask an AI assistant (ChatGPT, Google AI, Claude, Perplexity or your own) to summarize a page.
A row of buttons, action icons and selects that is one tab stop, moved through with the arrow keys.
Sections over an enum, each a heading whose button opens its panel, with one or many open.
A strip of slides that snaps as it scrolls and knows which one it is on, with controls, indicators and optional autoplay.
A gallery of pictures with optional caption bars, laid out on a GridZone, so cols counts the library's twelve tracks.
A person as a fixed square, with a fallback chain from a picture down to a person glyph, and a group that collapses its overflow into a +N chip.
A short status label, one uppercase pill with no role and no interaction.
A <dl> of term/description pairs, where one term can carry several descriptions.
A sized, colored box around an svg, which takes the box's color through currentColor.
An inline svg drawn from SvgData, such as a lucide icon, in currentColor and with no size of its own.
Swaps the glyphs libero draws itself (chevrons, close, checks, ...), slot by slot, for everything below it; lucide by default.
An with a fallback source on load error, rounded corners and an optional click-to-zoom overlay.
An <audio> with libero's own controls, and the use_media hook behind them.
A <video> with libero's own controls, captions and fullscreen, on the use_media hook.
A dot or a small capped count pinned to something else with a Float, never read out itself.
A sortable data table built from a row type and a list of column definitions.
An ordered list of events drawn against a rail, with an active index colouring the bullets and connectors up to the current one.
A <ul> of <li> items without the browser's list styling, with themed gaps and nested indent.
Content that scrolls on its own in an endless loop, with a pause toggle and a still fallback under reduced motion.
Encodes a string as a scalable QR code, rendered as an inline SVG.
A list the user reorders by dragging a handle, by keyboard, or with move buttons. use_sortable and use_sortable_item do the same for your own markup.
A board of columns whose cards move by drag in a column or to another, by keyboard or move buttons in a column, and to another column by a Move to menu.
A tinted surface for something the reader has to know, with a title, an optional icon and close button, and a role that follows its color.
An indeterminate busy indicator: a ring, bars or dots. It stays silent, so a status region says the wait. Button, Combobox and FileField show it.
A hook plus a host: render Notifications {} once, and use_notifications() shows messages from anywhere, as an Alert or your own template over your data.
A determinate or indeterminate progress bar over any min..=max range.
A placeholder for loading content, as a standalone grey shape or a wrapper that hides the real content until it is ready.
How to build libero forms, with specialized fields, composed parts, validators at each layer, typed paths from #[derive(Fields)] and binding.
A text field that offers completions from any Options type, while the value stays a String.
A checkbox with its label beside the box, the field slots under both, and an indeterminate state.
A compact token: a tag, a filter, a small action or a link.
A text field holding a ColorCode, with a preview swatch, an eyedropper and a ColorPicker in a dropdown.
A saturation panel and a hue slider, with optional alpha and preset swatches, over one ColorCode. Also documents HueSlider, AlphaSlider and ColorSwatch.
A listbox that hangs off a trigger you supply, holding no state of its own.
A text field for every date and time value, typed leniently, with the matching ChronoPicker in a dropdown.
One picker for every date and time value, from days, months and years to times, date-times and ranges of them.
Several fields that form one value under a <legend>, with rules over that value that land on the fields they name.
Files picked from the system dialog or dropped on the control, as a one-line input or a drop surface.
A <form> that validates on submit, with plain Fn(&V) -> bool rules, typed field paths from #[derive(Fields)] and a focused error summary.
A box with handles over an image, picking the part to keep by drag or arrow keys, free or at a fixed aspect, with a rect or circle mask.
A listbox over an enum that holds any number of its options, drawn as chips in the trigger.
A field that picks one option from a tree, one level at a time, and shows the path in the trigger.
A styled native <select> over an enum, with the field slots.
A numeric field over your own number type, with optional steppers in its trailing slot.
A TextField for secrets, with a button in its trailing slot that shows the text.
A country picker in front of a tel input, whose value is an E.164 string.
A pin, one character per cell, with auto-advance, paste spreading and an oncomplete that fires the moment the last cell fills.
A group of radios over an enum, exactly one selected, with one tab stop, arrow-key selection and the question as the group's name.
Two thumbs on one track, for a span instead of a point, over the same values as Slider.
A row of stars picking a value, whole or in halves, by click, sideways drag or arrow keys; read-only or display-only.
A rich text field over a Doc: headings, lists, quotes, code blocks and marks, with undo, shortcuts and Markdown typing.
A connected strip of segments over an enum, exactly one of them selected, with the field slots.
A listbox over an enum with rows you can draw yourself, in the same field frame as every other input.
A value dragged along a track, continuous over f64 or discrete over an ordered enum that derives SliderValue.
An on/off toggle drawn as a track and thumb, announced as a switch, with the field slots.
A field whose value is a Vec<String> of typed tags, drawn as chips around the input.
A single-line text field with a label, a description, helper text and a validation message.
A multi-line text field, sized by rows and resizable by the user.
Enforces a width-to-height ratio on its child, cropping it to fill the box.
The primitive every other component is built on, rendered as any tag via component and styled through sx.
Centers its child horizontally and vertically.
Animates its children's height open and closed, and follows the content when its height changes.
Centers content and caps its width at a breakpoint.
A horizontal or vertical rule, with an optional label sitting in the line.
A flexbox container with theme-aware direction, gap, alignment and wrapping.
Anchors its child to a corner or edge of the nearest positioned ancestor, like a badge on an avatar.
A layout matrix of named areas: Grid holds the shape, a GridZone is a twelve-column container with optional masonry, a GridItem takes a fraction of it.
The page's banner landmark, a sticky, static or fixed header bar for nav and actions.
The library's surface, with a background, a corner radius, an elevation and an optional hairline border, and no semantics of its own.
A scrollable region that fills its parent, with themed scrollbars, scroll positions in percent, edge events and row virtualization through Virtualize.
A horizontal strip with a hidden scrollbar and a step control over each end, shown while there is more content that way.
An in-flow panel on one edge of its parent that scrolls its own content, like a nav rail or an inspector.
Two panes split by a divider you can drag or move with the keyboard. Nest another Splitter in a pane for more than two.
Fades, slides or scales its children in on mount, and out when open turns false.
A phone's bar of three to five top-level destinations, each an icon over a label, the current one marked with aria-current.
Three bars that morph into an X, an ActionIcon with the ARIA a nav toggle needs.
A real link styled and sized like Text, router-aware through to.
A navigation list item for a sidebar or nav bar, a link that marks the current page with aria-current.
A row of page buttons in a named nav landmark, with an ellipsis that keeps the row the same width.
The stages of a process over an enum, horizontal or vertical, with the current step's content.
One strip of tabs over an enum, with only the selected tab's panel built.
A row of menus. Each menu is a Menu, and the bar is a single tab stop with one menu open at most.
A data-driven, keyboard-navigable tree view over your own node type.
The dialog surface with a header and role="dialog", which inside a modal also names and closes itself.
A dimmed, focus-trapped panel docked to one edge, use_modal with the docking around it.
A non-modal window over the page that drags, moves by keyboard and resizes from a corner, opened through a hook.
An interactive card that opens while its trigger is hovered or focused, a named, dismissible dialog on a paper surface.
A modal image viewer, use_modal with a gallery around it, with zoom, pan, captions and a thumbnail strip.
A list of commands that drops from a trigger, with groups, separators and submenus.
A hook that opens a render closure as a modal, with arguments and a result per opening.
A layer that dims and blurs the page behind it, with centred content. The backdrop behind a modal, or a loading screen.
A hook that anchors a portaled box to a trigger, flipping and shifting it to stay on screen.
A dialog listing keyboard shortcuts, each chord in the platform's key names.
A command palette. A modal search box over your actions, with groups, arrow-key highlight and a Ctrl/Cmd+K hotkey.
A label that appears while its child is hovered or focused by keyboard, portaled so nothing clips it.
A guided tour. A hook that dims the page around one element per step and explains it in a card beside it.
A quotation in a tinted frame with an accent bar, with the attribution outside the quote.
An inline <code> snippet, optionally syntax highlighted.
A multi-line code block with line numbers, a copy button, a language header, diffs and highlighted lines.
A single keyboard key, rendered as a real <kbd> and styled from the theme.
A mark element that highlights text with a light tint of a theme color.
Body copy, sized from the theme's text scale.
A heading, h1 through h6, whose visual size and semantic tag can be set apart.
